issue_context.title: Update Accessibility Model to use `wil`
issue_context.body:
# Description of the new feature/enhancement

We currently manually keep track of our own RefCount for our accessibility providers. This can cause improper RefCounts and updating, as well as improper transferring of ownership.

We should be using the `wil` library to fix these issues. Starting by making references `wil::com_ptr`s. This probably won't be too bad for Windows Terminal. We'll have to update some ConHost code too.
comments: Moving this out to 1911. Splitting it into a fix for #3209.

review_comments: With all these methods returning `HRESULT` now, _can_ they be `noexcept`? (if they can, I'm not saying do that now, just file follow-up CodeHealth work)

After checking that the pointer is valid (this line), you should set the value to `nullptr` to fill it up with the null value in case the `RETURN_IF_FAILED` is hit and an early return occurs. It's part of the Out SAL contract to always fill the result with *something* on all codepaths (presuming its a valid target location)
You will need to check and apply this pattern a bunch... I see a lot of instances of this.

In many cases... it doesn't look like you need to be using the temporary local in these functions at all. You could just be
1. check that the outpointer is valid
2. fill outpointer with null
3. call child function return if failed to fill up the outpointer
4. return S_OK
We need the temp var because `MakeAndInitialize` can't create a `UiaTextRangeBase`. Other than that, applied the feedback here.

So, this is all just a part of me deciding if we even need a WindowUiaProvider in Terminal. It's looking like we won't need it but I need to actually remove it at some point. Should I create a separate issue for this and link it?
I wonder if this is going to come back to bite us at some point. A **program-global** static ever-incrementing ID number?
It doesn't seem like we use _id anywhere, really, other than for debugging purposes. So we should be good.

So, in one of my commits, I tried having this as `LOG_IF_FAILED` instead of `THROW_IF_FAILED` and I'd get a crash on a creating a new tab. Specifically, the `UiaData` extracted from the `TermControl` would be `nullptr`, meaning that we wouldn't be able to really do any operations in the auto peer.

This fixed it by catching the crash. And we're still able to interact with the auto peer well on new tab/pane creation. I just feel lilke I might be missing a better fix. Thoughts?
